news.title: Hormuz Tanker Traffic Rises This Month Even as Attacks Increase
news.summary: Vortexa tracking shows more tankers crossed the Strait of Hormuz in November than the month before, even though strikes on ships in the area also climbed.
news.why: Rising transits despite more attacks mean war-risk premiums and fuel surcharges are likely to stay high, so importers should keep Gulf-linked freight quotes short-dated.

news.title: Crew Member Dies After Diesel Tanker Capsizes Off Ibiza, No Pollution So Far
news.summary: A small diesel tanker overturned and partly sank near Ibiza, killing at least one crew member, while Spanish officials say no fuel leak has been detected yet.
news.why: The incident is local, but it is a reminder for buyers of Balearic and western Mediterranean fuel deliveries to confirm backup supply arrangements during the salvage.

news.title: IMO Sounds Alarm Over Shortage of Training Berths for Future Seafarers
news.summary: The International Maritime Organization is pressing shipowners to offer more onboard places for cadets, warning that too few berths are holding back the next generation of officers.
news.why: A thinner pipeline of qualified crews pushes up ship operating costs over time, which eventually feeds into the ocean rates importers pay.

news.title: Italy Rebukes Ukraine Over Attacks on Russian Ships in Libya
news.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani criticised Kyiv for striking Russian vessels in Libyan waters and urged it not to carry the conflict into new regions.
news.why: Strikes spreading into the central Mediterranean could widen war-risk insurance zones, so shippers routing via Libyan or nearby ports should check cover terms.

news.title: PETA alleges animal abuse in PepsiCo's supply chain
news.summary: PETA filed a shareholder proposal on behalf of two PepsiCo investors claiming the company's sugar sourcing exposes it to animal-welfare risks.
news.why: Activist pressure is moving deeper into commodity supply chains, so food and beverage buyers should be ready to document how upstream ingredient suppliers operate.

news.title: EU Decision on Biocide Anti-Foulings Prompts Objection from Manufacturer
news.summary: Swedish firm I-Tech objected after EU member states voted against renewing approval of its anti-fouling biocide Selektope, arguing the move harms European shipyards and slows emissions cuts.
news.why: Buyers of marine coatings and shipyard services in Europe should check whether their current hull-coating products rely on biocides facing non-renewal and plan substitutes.

news.title: Frazier to build $20 million rack factory in Texas
news.summary: Frazier Industrial is investing $20 million in a semi-automated pallet-rack plant in Grand Prairie, Texas, due to open in March 2027 with about 130 jobs.
news.why: New domestic rack capacity in the Southwest could shorten lead times and cut freight costs for warehouse projects in Texas and nearby states from 2027.

news.title: Lithium-ion recycling market to reach $64 billion by 2047
news.summary: Research firm IDTechEx projects battery recycling will become a $64 billion market by 2047 as EV packs reach end of life, after capacity rose 77% between 2024 and 2026.
news.why: Fast-growing recycling capacity gives battery and electronics buyers a growing secondary source of lithium, nickel and cobalt to hedge against mined-supply shocks.

news.title: Déjà vu in Miami as FedEx MD-11 freighter overshoots runway
news.summary: A FedEx MD-11 cargo jet ran off the end of a Miami International runway in heavy rain, prompting a brief FAA ground stop but no injuries.
news.why: Miami is a key gateway for Latin American air cargo, so shippers with time-critical freight there should allow for short holiday-week delays and ask about MD-11 fleet availability.

news.title: 5 non-domiciled drivers want CDLs reinstated as battle separately moves through courts
news.summary: Five truck drivers who lost commercial licenses under the federal non-domiciled driver rule have petitioned for reinstatement while a court challenge to the rule is still pending.
news.why: The rule has pulled drivers out of the market, so the court outcome could loosen or tighten truckload capacity and spot rates heading into 2027 contract season.
